name: prof-f11-honda — extracted from f11-honda
palette: Muted neutrals with warm wood (honey, beige, pale brown) contrasted against cool silvers and blacks of metal, with a single accent color (red pedestal) reserved for the climax.
light_logic: Soft, even, daylight-like illumination with minimal shadows, consistent across shots to suggest a controlled, test-lab environment.
lens: Moderate focal lengths with low distortion, mostly level, side-on or three-quarter views that keep geometry legible and the chain’s direction easy to follow.
texture: Clean, polished metals and glass against smooth wooden floors and plain painted walls, avoiding dirt, grease, or clutter so the mechanism reads as intentional design, not workshop mess.
world: A single, bright, minimal interior room that feels like a calm studio or design lab, where everyday car parts are repurposed into a precise kinetic sculpture.
forbidden: Handheld or shaky camera that would obscure the clarity of the mechanism
Busy backgrounds or additional props that break the single-room, single-machine focus
Harsh, contrasty lighting that creates confusing shadows on the parts
Fast, chaotic cutting that makes the chain reaction hard to follow
Overt CGI or impossible physics that would undermine the sense of real-world reliability
